Cystic Fibrosis is a genetic condition worst known for affecting the airways and pancreas. It is caused by a mutated CFTR protein. The CFTR protein normally acts as a Cl- channel allowing Cl- to be secreted out of epithelial cells on their way to the surface. This draws water out of the body by osmosis and secreted by duct cells in the lungs, salivary glands, sweat glands and pancreas. In cystic fibrosis less CFTR means less Cl- and water secreted so surfaces become dry and sticky.
